chapters.title: Chapter 2: Reading the Yield Curve and Rate Signals

lessons.title: Credit Spreads as an Early Warning System

body.text: Credit spreads price default risk before it shows up as a non-performing loan. A widening spread is the bond market's real-time verdict on future corporate distress, delivered well before the accounting catches up.

children.text: Lesson 2.1 covered the sovereign yield curve. This lesson covers the second leg of Chapter 2's rate and credit toolkit: credit spreads, the gap between what a company pays to borrow and what the government pays. India's corporate bond market is shallower than the US market discussed in the last lesson, a limitation this lesson does not paper over, but it is deep enough in the higher-rated segment to give a genuinely useful, and often earlier, read than equity markets or reported earnings.
What a Credit Spread Actually Measures

A credit spread is the yield on a corporate bond minus the yield on a G-Sec of the same maturity. It compensates the lender for everything the sovereign bond does not carry: default risk, the chance the company misses a payment; downgrade risk, the chance its rating gets cut before maturity; and liquidity risk, the chance the bond is hard to sell quickly without moving the price. When the spread widens, the market is demanding more compensation for one or more of these risks, and it is doing so before a default, a downgrade, or a liquidity crunch actually happens. That is precisely what makes it a leading indicator by the definition from Lesson 1.2: it prices a forward-looking risk, not a realised outcome.

children.text: The Rating Ladder Matters: Spreads Don't Widen Uniformly

markDefs.definition: A shift in investor demand away from lower-rated, riskier assets and toward higher-rated, safer ones during periods of stress, widening the gap between their yields even if the safer asset's yield itself barely moves.

children.text: The single most useful thing about credit spreads is that they do not move together across the rating ladder during stress. AAA spreads typically widen moderately. AA and A-rated spreads widen far more sharply, and paper rated below investment grade can simply stop trading altogether as buyers disappear rather than reprice, a

. This divergence, not just the absolute level of the AAA spread, is itself a signal: a rating-differential blowout (the AA-minus-AAA spread widening sharply even while AAA itself looks stable) is often the earliest visible sign of credit stress building beneath a calm-looking headline number.

children.text: Case Study: India's 2018-19 NBFC Credit Crunch

body.title: How a Credit Spread Signal Turned Into a Real Slowdown

events.title: IL&FS Defaults
events.description: A large, highly rated infrastructure financing group defaulted on its debt obligations, catching the market off guard given its prior credit ratings, and immediately widened spreads across the NBFC and housing finance space.

events.title: Spreads Widen, Mutual Funds Face Redemption Pressure
events.description: AA and lower-rated NBFC and HFC paper saw spreads widen sharply as debt mutual funds, large holders of this paper, faced redemption pressure and grew reluctant to roll over exposure, tightening funding access for the sector broadly.

events.title: A Second Large NBFC, DHFL, Comes Under Stress
events.description: Stress spread to another major housing finance company, reinforcing that this was a sector-wide funding crisis rather than a single company's idiosyncratic failure.

events.title: Policy Response and Spillover Into the Real Economy
events.description: The RBI and government introduced liquidity and partial credit guarantee measures to support NBFC funding. By this point, the credit crunch had already tightened lending across the broader economy, a contributing factor to the pre-Covid growth slowdown covered in Lesson 1.3.

body.text: This was a domestic, sector-specific credit event, not a global shock or a broad-based recession, yet it produced real macro spillover: tighter NBFC funding fed directly into slower credit growth economy-wide, one of the leading indicators from Lesson 1.2. Credit spreads caught this well before it showed up in GDP or IIP data, which is exactly the argument for watching them alongside the yield curve, not instead of it.

children.text: How to Read Spreads in Practice

Three things are worth tracking together, not any single one in isolation. The level and trend of the AAA spread tells you the baseline cost of credit for the safest borrowers. The AA-minus-AAA differential, the rating-quality spread, tells you whether risk appetite is narrowing even before the headline AAA number moves. And primary market issuance volumes, how much new corporate debt is actually getting placed, tell you whether stress has gone beyond pricing and into outright market access: a sharp drop in issuance, especially concentrated in lower-rated names, is often a sign that spreads alone are understating the real stress, because the weakest borrowers have simply stopped being able to issue at any price.

body.title: Read the Credit Data
body.scenario: Over two quarters, you observe: the AAA 5-year corporate spread over G-Secs has widened from about 50 to 90 basis points, the AA-minus-AAA differential has widened far more sharply, from about 60 to 180 basis points, and primary market issuance of AA and lower-rated paper has fallen by roughly 40% quarter-on-quarter, while AAA issuance volumes are largely unchanged.
body.prompt: What does this combination suggest is happening, and which part of the data is the strongest evidence for it?
body.modelAnswer: This pattern points to a credit-quality-specific stress event, closer to the 2018-19 NBFC crisis than to a broad-based, economy-wide slowdown. If this were a general growth scare, you would expect AAA spreads to widen meaningfully too, since even the safest borrowers get repriced in a genuine recession fear. Instead, AAA has widened only modestly while AA has widened three times as much and lower-rated issuance has nearly halved, which is the flight-to-quality pattern from this lesson: capital is fleeing risk within the credit market specifically, not fleeing the economy broadly. The strongest single piece of evidence is the AA-minus-AAA differential blowout combined with the issuance volume drop concentrated in lower-rated names, since that shows market access itself narrowing for weaker borrowers, not just a uniform repricing across the board.

body.title: Check Your Understanding
body.question: Why is a widening AA-minus-AAA spread differential often a more useful early signal than the AAA spread level on its own?
options: Because AAA bonds are not actually traded in India
Because the differential captures a shift in risk appetite specifically, which frequently starts widening before the safest-rated AAA spread itself moves noticeably
Because AA-rated companies always default before AAA-rated ones
Because the RBI only publishes data for AA-rated bonds
body.explanation: A flight to quality typically shows up first as investors demanding much more compensation for slightly lower-rated risk, widening the AA-AAA gap, while the AAA spread itself, being the safest tier, can stay comparatively calm even as stress is clearly building beneath it. Watching the differential catches this shift earlier than watching the AAA level alone.

body.text: This lesson presents a general framework for reading credit spreads, for educational purposes. Spread figures are illustrative approximations, and actual levels vary by data provider, tenor, and issuer. This is not investment advice; verify current spreads against CRISIL, ICRA, or FBIL data before relying on them professionally.

points: A credit spread compensates lenders for default, downgrade, and liquidity risk, and widens before that risk actually materialises, making it a genuinely leading indicator
Spreads do not widen uniformly across the rating ladder; AAA moves moderately while AA and lower-rated paper widens far more sharply during stress, a flight to quality
The 2018-19 NBFC crisis showed how a domestic, sector-specific credit event, caught early by widening spreads, fed into a real economy-wide credit crunch and growth slowdown

Watch the AAA spread level, the AA-minus-AAA differential, and primary issuance volumes together; a widening differential or a drop in lower-rated issuance can signal stress before the AAA level moves much
